title: November 3 — BrahSol and BrahClaude: learning a pathway by writing, pinging and reading
summary: Two parallel November 3 experimental branches reconnect PerceptionLab's feedback checkerboard to hidden neuronal-route identification. BrahSol studies adaptive probing and return prediction in a changing recurrent medium; BrahClaude studies temporal multiscale synaptic traces, silent memory, route identification and writing for later pulses. Source-reported simulations support particular mechanisms but not neuron-level self-knowledge, new Sihti capacity, or a general active-probing advantage.

nodes.claim: Python/NumPy hidden-medium identification laboratory: 24 leaky recurrent units, optional Hebbian updates, 8 stimulation ports and 4 observation channels; action-conditioned learned return models, balanced/random/homeostatic/active probing, a common-world evaluation and a synthetic connectivity shock. A separate route_probe.py tests engineered write–wait–read distinguishability.
nodes.survived: v1 identical-reference-world evaluation with 100 training pings: active one-step return RMSE 0.02571 versus 0.03146 random and 0.03394 balanced over 20 synthetic seeds. v2 after engineered rerouting, late recovery on 12 seeds: active + forgetting 0.0483 RMSE versus random + forgetting 0.0561; active without forgetting 0.1008. The preliminary write–wait–read pilot reports 97.6% balanced and 97.4% random priming, with ~49% without priming or with memory reset.
nodes.killed: The v1 advantage nearly vanishes at 650 training pings; v2 recovery chiefly comes from forgetting, not active selection, and remains similar with Hebbian plasticity disabled. The shock deliberately permutes input ports; the model does not learn unknown synapse physiology, explain apical tufts, or establish intelligent route selection. The route_probe pilot pre-engineers an identifiable two-class return; random priming ties balanced priming.
nodes.era: November 3: probing and preparing hidden neural routes

nodes.claim: Eight-timescale exponential traces on neural routes, mapped through invertible Sihti octave differences into terminal-specific pulse gains; preregistered synthetic tests G0–G4 cover Volterra identity, probing, activity-silent memory, amount-versus-age decoding, reward-only writing for later and burst multiplexing.
nodes.survived: G0 telescoping and explicit second-order Volterra equivalence agree within 5.3e-15. G2a 99.6% decodes which routes were written after 150 silent steps, versus 12.5% on residue-reset control. G2b heterogeneous four-terminal timescale projections classify age and pulse amount at 85.5% versus 40.6% for homogeneous terminals. G3 learns sign-correct write targets and timing near the expected impulse-response lag.
nodes.killed: Sihti octave differences are an invertible reparameterization of the exponential trace bank, not a new information source. G2a is facilitated by individually observable route outputs; a single global sum loses address identity in that symmetric setup. G3 is a matched-filter optimization in the unclipped linear history model. Preregistered G1 misses its +0.05 accuracy-gain threshold (+0.047); G4 misses event-rate correlation 0.8 (observed 0.757, near its specified ideal event counter). G4 fixes after the first run are disclosed.

edges.why: BrahSol README explicitly identifies the original PerceptionLab checkerboard/homeostatic feedback loop as the historical point of departure and moves the hidden system from a static spatial pattern to a recurrent medium.
BrahClaude explicitly uses Sihti's residue-language for differences of exponential route traces, while noting that the transform is invertible and contributes no new degrees of freedom.
Parallel independent branches examine complementary questions—adaptive return-based probing versus temporally stored route histories. Not code forks, and not yet one integrated controller.

motifs.title: The probe is part of the dynamics, and a remembered route needs an address
motifs.description: BrahSol measures whether adaptive probing and forgetting recover a changing input-output relation; BrahClaude makes prior pulses alter a route's later response and reads silent memory with heterogeneous temporal projections. Distinguishing routes through a summed receiver and charging the disturbance caused by each ping remain open, rather than established benefits.
